rationale:
Evidence: iteration 9 (sensor_size 0.016, kp 1.8, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.1, narrow five-sensor array) is the best raced design at 403.3. The oval finished 20 of 20 with line_loss_events 0.15 and max_error 0.038. The s-bend still ends off track in all 20 runs, with line_loss_events at 2.0 and progress 0.55. The slalom is stuck at about 0.10 progress with line loss at 1.0.

The Evaluator's condition for the next step is met: the oval held at 20 of 20 while s-bend line loss stayed at 2.0. The requested single change is kp 1.8 to 1.6, with sensor_size 0.016 held. The kp trend (2.5 to 2.0 to 1.8) has cut line loss and raised completion on every track so far. The footprint change is kept, since it is what lifted the oval from 18 to 20 finishes.

Change: kp 1.8 to 1.6 only. Geometry (narrow five-sensor array at x = 0.03, 0.015, 0, -0.015, -0.03, y = 0.05, sensor_size 0.016), sensor_weights [2,1,0,-1,-2], base_speed 1.1, kd 0.3, ki 0 and last_direction are unchanged.

Expected result: oval stays at or near 20 of 20 with line loss about 0.15 to 0.3, and s-bend line loss falls below 2.0 with more progress. Risk: kp 1.6 may be too weak on the tightest bends, which would show as higher max_error and line loss on the oval.

Fallback: if oval completion drops below 18 of 20 or oval max_error rises above 0.044, revert to kp 1.8 (the iteration 9 design). Because this is the final iteration, the design should be robust on unseen tracks, so I have kept the change to one variable.

Hypotheses: (a) kp reduction continues to cut over-correction-driven line loss on the s-bend and slalom; (b) the 16 mm footprint keeps the oval stable at lower kp. Measurements requested: completion, progress, completion_time, line_loss_events, max_error and steering_oscillation on each track, plus noise_robustness, compared against the iteration 9 baseline.
